references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, the offering for the poor who cannot afford the regular sacrifice is described: two turtledoves or two young pigeons as a sin offering and a burnt offering.
A provision stating that whoever cannot afford a lamb may offer two turtledoves or two young pigeons—one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering.
Further provisions regarding offerings based on financial ability, where the priest makes atonement for the sin.
A similar provision for women after childbirth who cannot afford a lamb; she may bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons.
Description of the priest's act of atonement in the purification ritual, parallel to verse 31.
Basic provisions concerning burnt offerings from birds (turtledoves or young pigeons).
Mary and Joseph brought an offering according to the Lord’s law: a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons, showing that they followed the provision for the poor.
